mainTopic: Checking a בכור's מום on יום טוב, the ban on causing a מום, moving a dead animal on יום טוב, and dividing an animal without setting prices
overview: The גמרא finishes describing how רבא handled a בכור brought to him near יום טוב. He looked at the מום on ערב יום טוב, and on יום טוב itself he only asked how it happened, to rule out that the owner caused it. A ברייתא then proves from the words 'כל מום' that even indirectly causing a מום (גרמא) is forbidden. Next, a new משנה rules that a dead animal, and חלה that became טמא, may not be moved on יום טוב. The גמרא asks whether this משנה goes against רבי שמעון, who allows feeding a dead animal to dogs, and works through two reports of רבא's view of him. זעירי explains that the משנה is about a קדשים animal, which cannot be given to dogs, and the case is narrowed to an animal that was already in danger before יום טוב, so everyone agrees. Finally, a new משנה forbids signing up for shares of an animal on יום טוב. The גמרא explains that this means naming a price. רב shows how to divide the animal by comparing it to a matching one, and a ברייתא allows naming a fraction of the animal but not a sum of money.

steps.title: On יום טוב רבא only asked how it happened
steps.stepSummary: On יום טוב itself, רבא did not examine the בכור. He only asked how the מום came about.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on יום טוב he would only ask: how did the incident happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes describing רבא's method. On יום טוב he would not inspect the animal. He would only ask the owner how the מום happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inspecting a בכור's מום on יום טוב is a problem, because it is like 'fixing' the animal so it may be eaten. So רבא did the actual looking before יום טוב. Asking the owner a question is just talking, so he could do that on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And on the Festival he would only ask
how the incident happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the description of רבא's practice that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may only ask how the מום happened. The physical inspection must already have been done before יום טוב.

steps.title: The story: רבא sees the blemish on ערב יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A man brought a בכור to רבא toward evening on ערב יום טוב. רבא, while washing his hair, glanced up, saw the מום, and told the man to come back tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in the case of a certain man who brought a firstborn before רבא toward evening on ערב יום טוב. רבא was sitting and washing his head. He raised his eyes and saw its blemish. He said to him: Go now, and come back tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story that shows רבא's method in action. This is the first half: the looking happens on ערב יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sees the מום before יום טוב begins, so the inspection is already done. He sends the man away until tomorrow, which is יום טוב, when only the follow-up question will remain.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב יום טוב, the day before the Festival

phrases.english: As in that case of a certain man
who brought a firstborn before Rava
toward evening on the eve of the Festival.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה יָתֵיב רָבָא וְקָא חָיֵיף רֵישֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: Rava was sitting and washing his head.
He raised his eyes and saw its blemish.
He said to him: Go now
and come back tomorrow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the practice described in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's practice of inspecting before יום טוב.

steps.title: On יום טוב רבא asks how it happened
steps.stepSummary: The man came back on יום טוב, and רבא asked him how the מום happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came the next day, רבא said: How did the incident happen?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רבא's method. On יום טוב he asks his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא needs to know whether the מום came about naturally or whether someone made it happen on purpose. The answer decides whether the animal may be slaughtered because of this מום.

phrases.english: When he came the next day,
he said: How did the incident happen?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא לִמְחַר, אֲמַר: הֵיכִי הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story on the following day, which is יום טוב.

steps.title: The owner explains the thorn fence
steps.stepSummary: Barley was lying on one side of a thorn fence and the animal was on the other side. It pushed its head through to eat, and a thorn split its lip.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Barley was scattered on one side of a thorn fence, and the animal was on the other side. When it wanted to eat, it pushed its head through, and a thorn split its lip.
steps.whatsHappening: The owner answers רבא's question and describes how the מום happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From this description the מום looks accidental: the animal hurt itself while reaching for food. But the barley's position raises a doubt, which leads straight into רבא's next question.

phrases.english: He said to him: Barley was scattered
on this side of a thorn fence,
and it (the animal) was on the other side.
When it wanted to eat,
it pushed its head in
and a thorn split its lip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal cut its lip on a thorn while reaching for barley on the other side of a fence.

steps.title: רבא asks if the owner caused it
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: maybe you set this up on purpose to cause the מום?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps you caused it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא checks whether the owner deliberately put the barley there so that the animal would hurt itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Indirectly causing a מום (גרמא) is forbidden. If the owner did that, the מום would not let him slaughter the בכור. So this is the real point of 'asking how it happened.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְמָא אַתְּ גְּרַמְתְּ לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps you caused it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְמָא אַתְּ גְּרַמְתְּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the owner's description.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the owner deliberately caused the מום.

steps.title: The owner says no
steps.stepSummary: The owner answers that he did not cause it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The owner denies causing the מום, so the story ends with the מום counting as accidental.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the owner says he did not set it up, the מום was not deliberately caused, and the animal may be treated as blemished. The story now raises a question: where do we learn that causing a מום is forbidden at all?
steps.whatToRemember: רבא inspected the בכור before יום טוב and, on יום טוב, only asked how the מום happened, mainly to rule out the owner having caused it.

phrases.english: He said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner did not cause the מום.

steps.title: Where do we learn that causing a blemish is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that indirectly causing a מום is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that causing a blemish is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to ask for a source. It is setting up the next step, where a ברייתא will be quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's question assumed that גרמא of a מום is forbidden. The גמרא wants to know where this rule comes from, since the פסוק only seems to forbid a direct מום.

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that causing (a blemish) is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the assumption in רבא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source forbidding גרמא of a מום.

steps.title: A ברייתא asks about causing a blemish through something else
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק 'מום לא יהיה בו' and asks how we know one may not cause a מום indirectly, for example by putting dough on the animal's ear so that a dog will bite it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'There shall be no blemish in it.' This only teaches that it should not have a blemish. From where do we know that he may not cause it a blemish through something else, for example that he should not bring dough or a dried fig and put it on its ear so that a dog will come and take it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as its source. This step lays out the ברייתא's question and its example of an indirect מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק forbids making a מום directly. The ברייתא asks about a case where the person does not touch the animal at all. He only sets things up, and the dog does the damage.

keyTerms.meaning: as was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught:
"There shall be no blemish in it" (Vayikra 22:21);

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ מוּם,
phrases.english: I only know that it may not have a blemish;
from where do we know that one may not cause it
by means of something else,
that he not bring dough or a dried fig
and place it on its ear
so that a dog will come and take it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 7 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That גרמא of a מום is forbidden.

steps.title: The extra word 'all' includes indirect blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק's wording 'כל מום', any blemish. The extra word 'כל' includes causing a מום indirectly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'any blemish.' It said 'blemish,' and it said 'any blemish.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The added word 'כל' (any/all) widens the ban to include indirect causing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have said just 'מום', but it said 'כל מום'. That extra word teaches that every way of bringing about a מום is forbidden, including setting things up for a dog to cause it. This is the source behind רבא's question.
steps.whatToRemember: Causing a מום to a sacred animal, even indirectly (גרמא), is forbidden. We learn it from the extra word 'כל' in 'כל מום'.

phrases.english: The verse states: "any blemish."
It said "blemish," and it said "any blemish."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'כל' includes indirect causing of a מום.

steps.title: New משנה: a dead animal may not be moved
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that an animal that died on יום טוב may not be moved from its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An animal that died, one may not move it from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that if an animal died on יום טוב, you may not move it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance the reason is מוקצה: when יום טוב began the animal was alive, so nobody had it in mind as food for dogs. The גמרא will refine this in steps 16-19. There it explains that the animal is a קדשים animal that was already in danger before יום טוב, so it may not be moved because it cannot be given to dogs.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An animal that died —
one may not move it from its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: מוקצה on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that died on יום טוב may not be moved.

steps.title: רבי טרפון is asked about the dead animal and חלה that became טמא
steps.stepSummary: There was a real case: people asked רבי טרפון about a dead animal and about חלה that became טמא on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was an incident, and they asked רבי טרפון about it and about חלה that had become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story to back up its ruling. Two questions are put to רבי טרפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלה that became טמא may not be eaten, and it may not be burned on יום טוב, so it has no use that day. That puts it in the same situation as the dead animal.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of dough given to the כהן

phrases.english: And there was an incident, and they asked Rabbi Tarfon
about it and about challah that became impure,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story to support the ruling in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a dead animal, or חלה that became טמא, be moved on יום טוב?

steps.title: The חכמים rule: do not move them
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון went to the בית המדרש and asked, and the חכמים answered that neither item may be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He entered the בית המדרש and asked, and they said to him: One may not move them from their place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון brings the question to the בית המדרש, and the חכמים rule that both items must stay where they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither the dead animal nor the טמא חלה can be used on יום טוב, so both are מוקצה. The story confirms the משנה's opening ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב, a dead animal and חלה that became טמא may not be moved. The גמרא will explain that the animal here is a קדשים animal, forbidden for any benefit, just like the טמא חלה.

phrases.english: And he entered the study hall and asked,
and they said to him: One may not move them from their place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question put to רבי טרפון.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Neither the dead animal nor the טמא חלה may be moved.

steps.title: Does our משנה go against רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our unattributed משנה does not follow רבי שמעון, who allows cutting up a dead animal for dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Shall we say that our unattributed משנה does not follow רבי שמעון? As we learned: רבי שמעון says, one may cut up gourds for an animal, and a dead animal for the dogs. רבי יהודה says: if it was not already a dead animal before שבת began, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking whether our משנה, which forbids moving an animal that died on יום טוב, clashes with רבי שמעון's opinion in another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids an animal that died on שבת itself, which suggests that רבי שמעון permits even that animal. If so, רבי שמעון would allow moving an animal that died on the holy day. Our משנה forbids it, so it seems to go against רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed משנה, stated with no name attached
An animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shall we say we learned the unattributed mishna
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה from step 10, about an animal that died on יום טוב.

phrases.english: not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon?
As we learned: Rabbi Shimon says:
phrases.notes: This is quoted from a משנה in מסכת שבת.

phrases.english: One may cut up gourds for an animal,
and a carcass for the dogs.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה נְבֵלָה מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת — אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.english: If it was not a carcass from before Shabbat, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This implies that רבי שמעון permits even an animal that died on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תְּנַן סְתָמָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whose opinion the משנה of steps 10-12 follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The unattributed משנה forbidding the move of an animal that died on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון seems to permit an animal that died on the holy day, but the משנה forbids it. So the משנה appears not to follow רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees about animals that died suddenly
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי שמעון agrees that animals that were healthy and then died on the holy day are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון agrees that living animals that died are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה can still match רבי שמעון. Even he agrees that animals which were alive and well, and then died, are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's leniency covers an animal that was already sick before the holy day, since the owner expected to give it to the dogs. A healthy animal that died suddenly was never planned for that, so even רבי שמעון treats it as מוקצה. Our משנה is about that kind of animal.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Shimon,
Rabbi Shimon agrees about living animals
that died, that they are forbidden.
phrases.notes: This means animals that were healthy before the holy day and died suddenly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the משנה against the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון permits every animal that died on the holy day.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון only permits an animal that was sick beforehand. A healthy animal that died suddenly is forbidden even to him.

steps.title: A second report of רבא says רבי שמעון permits even these
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for one report of רבא's view, but not for the other report, which says רבי שמעון permits even animals that died suddenly.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to מר בר אמימר quoting רבא, who said רבי שמעון agrees that animals that died are forbidden. But according to מר בריה דרב יוסף quoting רבא, who said רבי שמעון disagreed even about animals that died and permits them, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 14. There are two reports of what רבא said, and the answer only fits one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר אמימר reports that רבי שמעון agrees about sudden deaths, so the answer works. מר בריה דרב יוסף reports that רבי שמעון permits even sudden deaths. According to that report, our משנה still clashes with רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: This works well according to Mar bar Ameimar
in the name of Rava, who said:
Rabbi Shimon would agree
about living animals that died, that they are forbidden. That is fine.
But according to Mar, son of Rav Yosef,
in the name of Rava, who said:
Rabbi Shimon disagreed
even about living animals that died, that they are permitted:
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 14 using a different report of רבא's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 14 that רבי שמעון agrees about animals that died suddenly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One report of רבא says רבי שמעון permits even sudden deaths. According to that report, the משנה still contradicts רבי שמעון.

steps.title: זעירי: the משנה is about a קדשים animal
steps.stepSummary: זעירי explains that the dead animal in the משנה was a holy, sacrificial animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי explained it as referring to a קדשים animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that works for everyone. The משנה is talking about an animal of קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One may not get any benefit from a dead קדשים animal, so it cannot be fed to dogs. It therefore has no use, and that is why it may not be moved. This has nothing to do with the argument about מוקצה, so even רבי שמעון agrees.
steps.confusionAlert: The reason here is not מוקצה. The animal is forbidden because it is holy and may not be used for any benefit, so even רבי שמעון's leniency does not help.

phrases.english: Ze'iri explained it:
as referring to a sacred animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by redefining the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about an ordinary animal, so it must disagree with רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a קדשים animal, which is forbidden for benefit, so it fits every view of רבי שמעון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This allows the unattributed משנה to fit רבי שמעון even if he is lenient about sudden deaths.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports זעירי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה pairs the animal with חלה, which is holy, so the animal must also be holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise this way, because it teaches: 'about it and about חלה that became טמא.' Just as חלה is holy, so too the animal is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports זעירי's answer from the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question put to רבי טרפון joined the dead animal together with טמא חלה. Since חלה is holy, the animal mentioned alongside it is most likely holy too. This fits זעירי's reading well.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise this way
The portion of dough given to a כהן, which is holy

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה forbids moving the dead animal because it is a קדשים animal, forbidden for any benefit. This is why it fits even רבי שמעון, and the pairing with חלה supports this reading.

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it teaches:
'about it and about the challah that became impure.'
phrases.notes: This quotes the case brought to רבי טרפון in step 11.

phrases.english: Just as challah is holy,
so too the animal is holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports זעירי's answer from step 16 using the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: זעירי's reading that the animal is a קדשים animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה pairs the animal with חלה, which is holy (step 11).

steps.title: If only a holy animal is forbidden, which report of רבא does this fit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that זעירי's answer implies a non-holy dead animal may be moved. That fits one report of רבא's view of רבי שמעון but clashes with the other report.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the only reason it is forbidden is that the animal was holy. A non-holy animal would be allowed. That works well for מר בריה דרב יוסף, who reported in the name of רבא that רבי שמעון permits even animals that died. But for מר בר אמימר, who reported in the name of רבא that רבי שמעון agrees that animals that died are forbidden, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what זעירי's answer implies and shows that this implication runs into a problem with one of the two reports of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal in the משנה is forbidden only because it was holy, then a regular dead animal would be allowed. That works if רבי שמעון permits even animals that died suddenly, as מר בריה דרב יוסף reports. But according to מר בר אמימר, רבי שמעון forbids animals that died, so the implied ruling matches no known opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is that it was holy
Living animals that died (on יום טוב)
What can be said? (a strong challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: Two different people report רבא's view of רבי שמעון. מר בריה דרב יוסף says רבי שמעון permits animals that died. מר בר אמימר says רבי שמעון agrees they are forbidden. The challenge here is only against the second report.

phrases.english: But then, the reason is that it was holy
which means a non-holy animal is permitted
phrases.notes: The inference drawn from זעירי's answer

phrases.english: This works well according to Mar, son of Rav Yosef
in the name of Rava, who said:
Rabbi Shimon disagreed
even about animals that died, saying they are permitted
that is fine.
But according to Mar bar Ameimar
in the name of Rava, who said:
Rabbi Shimon agreed
about animals that died, that they are forbidden
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דְּקַדִּישָׁא הָא דְּחוּלִּין שַׁרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes זעירי's answer (holy animal) and draws a consequence from it that causes a new problem
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's explanation that the משנה's animal was holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The explanation implies a non-holy dead animal is permitted. That contradicts מר בר אמימר's report that רבי שמעון forbids animals that died, so the משנה would fit no one.

steps.title: The case is an animal that was already in danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about an animal that was already close to dying before יום טוב, and in that case all agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? An animal that was in danger of dying, and this is everyone's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case: the animal was already sick and in danger before יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an animal is already in danger before יום טוב, the owner expects it to die and plans in advance to give it to his dogs. So even the strict report of רבי שמעון agrees a non-holy animal like this may be moved. Only a holy animal stays forbidden, because it cannot be fed to dogs at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (the גמרא narrows the case)
An animal in danger of dying

steps.whatToRemember: The dead-animal section ends this way: the משנה speaks of a holy animal that was already in danger before יום טוב. A non-holy animal in danger may be moved for dogs according to everyone. A holy one is forbidden because it cannot be given to dogs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the key idea behind מוקצה here: if a person had the animal in mind before יום טוב, it is not set aside, so it may be used.

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing here?
With an animal in danger of dying, and it is everyone's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה was about an animal that died suddenly, so the implied permission for a non-holy animal clashed with מר בר אמימר's report.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about an animal already in danger before יום טוב. In that case even the strict view agrees a non-holy one is permitted.

steps.title: New משנה: signing up for shares of an animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that you may not sign up for a share of an animal on יום טוב itself, but you may sign up the day before and then slaughter and divide it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not sign up for shares of an animal on יום טוב at the start. But one may sign up for it on ערב יום טוב, and then they slaughter it and divide it among themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about a group of people splitting one animal on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Signing up for shares on יום טוב looks like doing business, which is a weekday activity. If the group arranged the shares the day before, the business part already happened, so on יום טוב they only slaughter and divide.

keyTerms.meaning: Signing up or registering for a share
At the start, before the fact

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not register for shares of an animal
at the start, on a Festival.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִמְנִין עָלֶיהָ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: But one may register for it from the eve of the Festival,
and they slaughter it and divide it among themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין נִמְנִין עַל הַבְּהֵמָה לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the dead-animal discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Signing up for shares of an animal is forbidden on יום טוב but allowed on ערב יום טוב. Slaughtering and dividing may then be done on יום טוב.

steps.title: What does 'not registering' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly is forbidden when the משנה says you may not sign up for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'one may not register' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the משנה's phrase, which sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נמנין is unclear. It could mean joining the group at all, or it could mean something more specific. The גמרא wants to pin down exactly which act is forbidden.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the meaning of 'one may not register'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the new משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact act forbidden by the term נמנין

steps.title: It means not setting prices
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, explains that the forbidden act is fixing a price for the animal's shares on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: One may not fix prices at the start for an animal on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'registering' means setting a money price for each share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joining the group is not the problem. The problem is naming a price, because that makes it a business deal on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One may not fix a price at the start
for an animal on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נמנין means fixing a money price for shares. That is what is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: So how can they divide it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how people can divide an animal on יום טוב if they may not set prices.
steps.simpleTranslation: How should one do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a practical method, which sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no price may be named, the buyers still need some fair way to know what each will pay later. The גמרא asks how this works in practice.

phrases.english: How should he do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the ban on fixing prices in step 22
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical way to divide the animal fairly without fixing a price

steps.title: Compare the animal to a matching one
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the seller places two animals side by side and asks whether this one is like that one. After יום טוב they price the matching animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: He brings two animals, stands them next to each other, and says: Is this one like that one?
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a way to divide the animal fairly on יום טוב without ever naming a price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyers agree that the slaughtered animal equals the other animal in value. After יום טוב, they set a price on the living animal, and that tells them what each person owes. No money talk happens on יום טוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He stands them next to each other
This one is like that one

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב you may not set prices for shares of an animal. You may compare it to a matching animal and settle the price after יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rav said: He brings two animals
and stands them one next to the other,
and says: Is this one equal to that one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the practical question of step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Compare the animal to an identical one without naming a price, then price the matching animal after יום טוב.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the ban on naming a price
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on יום טוב a person may not join an animal purchase by naming a sum of money, like a סלע or two סלעים. He may join by naming a fraction of the animal, like half, a third, or a quarter. This supports שמואל's explanation that the forbidden act is fixing a price.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: A person should not say to his friend on יום טוב, 'I am in with you for a סלע' or 'I am in with you for two סלעים.' But he may say to him, 'I am in with you for half,' or 'for a third,' or 'for a quarter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as outside support for what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל. The ברייתא clearly separates naming money, which is forbidden, from naming a share size, which is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I'm in for a סלע' sets a price, which looks like buying and selling on יום טוב. Saying 'I'm in for half' only sets how much of the animal you get, and no money is mentioned. The price is fixed after יום טוב, which fits both שמואל's explanation and רב's method of comparing two animals.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught so.' This introduces a ברייתא that supports the statement just made.
'I am hereby with you.' This means I am joining you as a partner in this animal.
A silver coin. Here it stands for naming a money price for your share.
For half. This is a share of the animal, not an amount of money.
A third and a quarter. These are more fraction-shares that are allowed to be named.

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב you may say WHAT PORTION of the animal you are taking, such as half, a third, or a quarter. You may not say HOW MUCH MONEY you will pay, such as a סלע. The money gets settled after יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'בְּסֶלַע' as a size of share. It is a money amount, a price, and that is exactly why it is forbidden. Half, a third, and a quarter are allowed because they are portions of meat, not prices.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical line for partnerships in food on יום טוב. You may divide up the food, but you must not do anything that looks like a business deal with a price.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא):
phrases.notes: Formula bringing outside support from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: A person may not say to his friend
phrases.notes: The setting is יום טוב, when the animal is about to be slaughtered.

phrases.english: 'I am hereby with you for a sela,'
phrases.notes: He names a money amount, which is setting a price.

phrases.english: 'I am hereby with you for two (sela'im),'
phrases.notes: Another example of naming a price.

phrases.english: But he may say to him:
phrases.notes: Now the ברייתא turns to what is permitted.

phrases.english: 'I am hereby with you for half,'
phrases.notes: He names a portion of the animal, not money.

phrases.english: or for a third, or for a quarter.
phrases.notes: More examples of allowed fraction-shares. The price is set after יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב explained how to divide the animal without setting prices (step 24), the גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the basic rule of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל (step 22): price-fixing on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל's explanation that the משנה's ban on 'signing up' for an animal means fixing a price on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbids saying 'I'm with you for a סלע or two' and permits saying 'I'm with you for half, a third, or a quarter.'
